## Hamlet Linguistic Analysis

This is a full text analysis project using dialogue from Shakespeare's play Hamlet. I analyze character strings to answer the following 2 research questions: Who is the biggest yapper (i.e. who talks the most) in Hamlet? How does language about love compare to language about death?

#### Load/Clean Data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)
library(plotly)

hamlet <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-09-17/hamlet.csv')

hamlet <- hamlet |>
  filter(
    !str_detect(
      character,
      regex("stage direction", ignore_case = TRUE)
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(dialogue), !is.na(character))
```


### Question 1: Who speaks the most in each Act?
```{r}
# Count words in each phrase.
hamlet_words <- hamlet |>
  mutate(
    word_count = str_count(
      dialogue,
      "\\b[[:alpha:]]+\\b"
    )
  )

# Add words per character, per act. 
act_words <- hamlet_words |>
  group_by(act, character) |>
  summarise(
    total_words = sum(word_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

#### Plot (Stacked Bar Chart)
```{r}
act_plot <- ggplot(
  act_words,
  aes(
    x = act,
    y = total_words,
    fill = fct_reorder(character, -total_words, .fun = sum),
    text = paste0(
      "Act: ", act,
      "<br>Character: ", character,
      "<br>Words: ", total_words
    )
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Who Speaks the Most in Each Act of Hamlet?",
    x = "Act",
    y = "Total Words Spoken",
    fill = "Character"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(act_plot, tooltip = "text")
```
